messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] predict in colext
messages.body_plain:
Hi Paul,

Your first question is about R not unmarked. The error comes from trying to create a data.frame with vectors of different lengths. I think you need to use rep() to expand your character vectors:

nd <- data.frame(a=1:4, b=rep(c("x", "z"), each=2))

Your second question seems to be related to prediction. This is too big a topic to cover here. A book on regression should be helpful, and there is some (rather bad) info here: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prediction_interval under the "Regression analysis" section. The predict function in unmarked does not provide estimates of equilibrium occupancy. However, you can compute such things yourself. Marc Kéry was kind enough to write the bulk of a new vignette that will eventually be part of unmarked. It should help. You can find it here: https://sites.google.com/site/unmarkedinfo/home/misc-files.

Best,
Richard

On Tue, May 31, 2011 at 7:42 PM, PaulS <pasch...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hello,
>  I have a couple questions regarding the use of the predict function
> for colext models.  I have already run the same set of candidate
> models for 20 different species and now want to interpret results and
> make some general comparisons across species.
>
> Number of sites=228
> Number of Primary sampling periods (i.e. years) = 7
> Number of Secondary occasions (i.e. number of visits per year) = 7
>
> #Some of the variables:
> dry.site (days into dry season): continuous, range 0-150
> water.site (dist to water): continuous, range 0-8000
> boma.site(dist to human settlement): continuous, range: 0-10500
> use.yr (land use): categorical, "buffer", "ca", "graze", "perm"
>
> # The all years data frame, this is an unmarkedMultiFrame object for
> one species (ex. bate).
> umf <- unmarkedMultFrame(bate.history, site.cov.formatted,
> obs.cov.formatted, numyears, site.year.cov.formatted)
>
> #Although each species was found to have it's own top models, I also
> found a single model that was well-supported across all species (model
> with the highest cumulative weight across species) to use for general
> comparisons:
>
> single.model <- colext(~scale(dry.site)+scale(water.site)
> +scale(boma.site), ~use.yr, ~use.yr, ~occ.obs+year.obs, umf)
>
> 1. I was able to get all of my models to run properly, but am now
> having difficulties with the predict function.  Here is the code I
> tried to use, but got an error.  Any ideas on how to get the lengths
> of the continuous and categorical variables to match up?
>
> top.nd <- data.frame(dry.site=seq(0, 150, length=228),
> water.site=seq(0, 8000, length=228),
>    boma.site=seq(0, 10500, length=228),
>    use.yr=c("buffer","ca","graze","perm"),
>    occ.obs=c("1","2","3","4","5","6","7"),
>    year.obs=c("1","2","3","4","5","6","7"))
> top.predict <- predict(single.model, type="psi", newdata=top.nd,
> appendData=TRUE)
>
> Error in data.frame(dry.site = seq(0, 150, length = 228), water.site =
> seq(0,  :
>  arguments imply differing number of rows: 228, 4, 7
>
> 2. When I have worked through simpler colext models, I got estimates
> for the beta's and SE's for initial occ, col, ext, det.  For our
> study, we are primarily interested in determining which variables most
> influence overall occupancy across species. From what I gather (and
> maybe I'm wrong), 'predict' provides an overall or equilibrium
> occupancy which accounts for everything you specify in the model.
> However, the predicted occupancy doesn't provide anything for
> comparison across species like your beta's do.  I saw in a paper in
> Sciency by Ferraz et al (2007) where they created a metric that was a
> ratio of the estimated values of occupancy from the smallest value of
> the covariate to the largest, and made comparisons across species that
> way.  Do you think this is the best option or is there another way I
> can obtain some estimate for comparison?
>
> I would really appreciate everyone's insight...  I've made my way
> through a lot of the earlier coding issues through your advice in the
> forum.  This is a great way to learn.  Thanks in advance for your
> help.
>
>
>

messages.subject: job opportunity
messages.body_plain:
Dear unmarked users,

Please pass this job announcement around. Thanks!

Richard

_____________________________________
Richard Chandler, post-doc
USGS Patuxent Wildlife Research Center
301-497-5696

Student Research Assistant Needed
Quantitative Ecology – Mathematical/Statistical Modeling, R programming, Data Analysis

USGS PATUXENT WILDLIFE RESEARCH CENTER

The Quantitative Ecology Group at USGS Patuxent Wildlife Research Center is searching for an extremely motivated and talented research assistant to assist with the development of the R package “unmarked” (http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/index.html) part-time during 2011 and possibly continuing into 2012, or full-time during the summer or fall 2011 (approx. 12-20 weeks).
The position involves data analysis, code testing, and preparing tutorials and other package documentation. Knowledge of the R programming environment is required. Must be highly motivated and able to work independently. Other desired skills include experience with R package development, S4 object-oriented programming, likelihood methods of statistical inference, LaTeX document preparation, and experience with hierarchical models of animal occurrence and abundance as described in Royle and Dorazio (Academic Press 2008). The source code of the package can be inspected here: https://github.com/rbchan/unmarked.

The position requires completion of a B.S. degree in any related field. The ideal candidate is a current graduate student in Ecology, Natural Resources or Statistics, and interested in the application of quantitative methods to ecological problems as an element of his or her graduate research.

Students are responsible for all costs of transportation to and from Patuxent Wildlife Research Center. Compensation is approx.. $18-$23 / hr depending on qualifications.

Principal Duty Station:
USGS Patuxent Wildlife Research Center
12100 Beech Forest Road
Laurel, Maryland 20708-4038

To apply, send the following to Andy Royle at the above address or via email (aro...@usgs.gov) or FAX (301.497.5545):

1) Letter of interest, professional interests, and career goals (if any).
2) Piece of R code that does something interesting, useful, efficiently, or in a novel way. (also describe what it does, just in case).
3)  Resume, including relevant experience, list of relevant classes, contact information and two or three reference contacts

messages.subject: AICcmodavg with unmarkedFit classes
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

For those interested, the latest version of package AICcmodavg (1.16),
which can be used to conduct model selection and multimodel inference,
now supports the classes unmarkedFitOccu,  unmarkedFitColExt,
unmarkedFitPCount, unmarkedFitPCO, and unmarkedFitOccuRN.  I also
included functions to model-average parameter estimates with or
without shrinkage for such models. The functions feature "exclude"
arguments so that model-averaging is conducted correctly in the case
of main effects involved in interactions in some models. The package
is available on CRAN.

I really like the unmarked package - nicely done!  Features to fix
parameter estimates would be really nice.

Best,

Marc

Hi Carlos,

Your continuous covariate "forest.nat" is being treated as a factor by R (ie a categorical variable). Try importing the data using something like:

Then try standardizing "forest.nat". Starting values should not be necessary.

Hope this works,
Richard

mydata <- read.csv(blah.csv, dec=",")
